lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Emberwick, at the Ashen Ford. The ground is warm underfoot, and the river steams in the evening cold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It used to be warmer. Nobody in town will say so.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: You came! I told Bree you'd come. The mayor's been asking for you all day, and he's ever so cross.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Pip, let them breathe. You lot, there's stew when he's done with you. Don't let him talk it cold.
lines.direction: calling from the inn door, brisk and fond

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Friends. Thank you for coming. I'd shake every hand, but the light's going, and so is our grain.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: The Skarrow goblins took the ford bridge nine days ago. It's our only road east, and every cart of winter flour comes over it.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Killed two of my guards doing it. Coll and Annet. Good people.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: The new moon is eleven days off. After that the last carts stop running, and Emberwick starts eating its seed corn.

options.label: Who are these goblins?
You've got me, Halden. What does the town need?
Captain. I was on that bridge with you.
Lady Marrowby asked me to keep an eye on things.
Pip. Have you been sleeping?
Show us the bridge.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: A hill clan. Their chief is an old woman they call Mother Skarrow. I've never met her, and I don't need to.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Forty winters she's led them. Clever. She'll smile at you while her archers find the range.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: She sent a little one down for bread in the spring. Asked at the granary gate, polite as you like.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Bree. Not now.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: There. That's what I hoped to hear. They still tell the story of you in this square, you know.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: People will be calmer if it's you who goes. Calm matters this winter. More than you'd think.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Calm's for after. Bridge first.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Aye. You were. Not many of us walked off it.
lines.direction: softer than usual, then flat again

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: You saw what they did. When the time comes, you tell them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You remember that morning. You remember it differently than she does.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Did she. Of course she did. Tell her the town is handling it. And tell her kindly, would you?
lines.direction: quiet and fast, the smile slipping

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: The Marrowbys have been very generous to Emberwick. Very generous. We are all very grateful.
lines.direction: back to the public voice, too quickly

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Course I have. Mostly.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I dreamed the river was boiling again. Again's the wrong word, isn't it? I wasn't there.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Bad dreams and too much cheese, that's all. In you come, Pip. Bed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the square, someone in a deep hood leans in the doorway of the Last Coal. They have not touched the cup in their hand.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: That one came the same week as the goblins. Never eats. Never sleeps that I've seen. Bree says it's rude to stare.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Go and look at your bridge. It's older than your town, and it has seen this before.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Come down to the bridge end with me. You should see what we're up against before you tell me anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the town's end of the ford bridge, the old Warden stones are slick with steam. Goblin fires burn on the far bank.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Small figures move between them. Fewer than you expected. Thinner.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: There. Forty of them, perhaps. Dagna has eight guards left. And she has you.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Hit them at dawn, from both banks. They'll break. Goblins always break.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: And the ones who don't break, Dagna? The ones with nowhere left to run to?
lines.direction: she has followed them down with a basket

options.label: Why did they take the bridge?
Your guards shot first, Captain. At children.
Make your cases. Both of you.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Hunger, I expect. It's been a lean year for everyone, and the hills are always harder than the valley.
lines.direction: smooth, a speech he has given before

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Leaner for them. We had the warm fields. They had snow on their fires by the Harvest Month.

options.label: There's something he isn't saying.
Fair enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He answers a heartbeat too fast, and he does not look at the granary roofs behind him.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Whatever you think you see, it can wait until the bridge is ours. Please.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Trust me, friends. If there were a simpler answer, I'd have found it years ago.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Say that again.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Coll always had a nervous bow hand. I sent him out at first light because I trusted him. Children.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Two of mine are still dead. But I'll want a better reason than hunger now, and I haven't got one.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Oh, Dagna.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Here's mine. Every day we talk, the road stays shut. Talk is a luxury, and we've eleven days of it.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: They chose spears over asking. Answer the spears, and the next hungry clan knows what that bridge costs.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: And here's mine. That's a whole people up there, and they're hungry for the same reason we are, only worse.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Kill their mother and you've bought a bridge for one winter. Her grandsons will remember it for fifty.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Either way, I need that road. I'd like it quick, and I'd like it cheap. I'm not sure I can have both.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: The ford is the only road east. If those goblins hold the bridge past the new moon, Emberwick goes hungry this winter.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Will you clear them out, or will you talk to their chief?

options.label: We'll clear the ford by force.
We'll go and parley with the chief.
First, what's it worth to you?

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Ha. My mother would have liked you. Forty crowns from the town chest, and the Last Coal's best rooms till spring.
lines.direction: caught out, then laughing it off

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: My best rooms. He means my only rooms. Still. Done.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: It's worth Emberwick. I'm afraid that's all I can pay you with that isn't already promised to someone.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Twenty crowns. My own. Now choose.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: So. Spears, or words? Whatever you choose, I'll stand behind it.

options.label: We'll clear the ford by force.
We'll go and parley with the chief.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Good. Dawn, then, from both banks. I'll have the guards in the reeds before first light.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: I'll keep the stew warm. For whoever comes back across.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Thank you. Truly. Emberwick won't forget this.
lines.direction: sincere; the irony is lost on him

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Talk, then. When she puts a spear through you, remember who told you she would.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Promise her nothing. Do you understand me? Nothing about the granaries.
lines.direction: quiet and fast, a hand on someone's sleeve

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Bread. Two days old, but it's honest. Take it up the hill. Children first, mind.
lines.direction: pressing a heavy basket into someone's arms

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The path into the Skarrow Hills is frozen mud. The camp at the top is smaller than anyone in town imagined.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Children watch you from the hide tents. They are too quiet, and their wrists are too thin.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Valley people. Walking. Not running at me with spears. This is new.
lines.direction: cracked and rasping; slow, deliberate valley tongue, as a courtesy

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: You lock your grain and call us thieves. Sit. We will talk about who stole what.

options.label: We brought bread. For the children.
I'll greet her in the hill tongue.
I was on the bridge the day it was taken.
Give us the bridge, and we'll talk about grain.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Two-day bread. From the innkeeper, yes? The one who feeds anybody.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Small kindness. Small stomachs. It is not nothing.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Ha! Somebody's mother taught you properly. You say my name like you have been scolded with it.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Then you know a hill word the valley does not have. It means a debt that both sides pretend is a gift.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Then you saw. My little ones were down on the bank, digging roots. Your people shot at them.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: We took the bridge after. Not before. Tell your captain that, if she will hear it.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Here is the bargain, and it is a short one. Your town eats. My clan eats. The bridge goes back to being a bridge.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Not coin. Coin does not boil. A share of the grain your mayor keeps behind his locks. Every week, until the thaw.

options.label: A share of the grain. You have our word.
Half now, the rest when the road is open.
Can you hold your own warriors to this?

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Half now, half at the thaw. You bargain like a hill grandmother. I will take it, and I will watch you.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Half? My children do not eat half. All of it, every week, or go home and fetch your captain.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: But you climbed the hill. So. Sit down again, and agree with me.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Most of them. Some of the young ones belong to my grandson now, in their hearts. Vorga. He left us to take instead of ask.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: His friends will not like a truce. If they bare their teeth on the bridge, do not kill more of them than you must.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Forty winters I have held this clan. Do not ask me if I can hold it one more.
lines.direction: too sharp, and she knows it

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Then it is agreed. Tell your mayor the old mother will give back his bridge. Tell him she is counting the sacks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She offers a hand, small and hard as a root. When you take it, the children in the tents begin, at last, to whisper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dawn. Mist lies thick on the steaming river, and Dagna's guards wait in the reeds of both banks.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: I see you, valley people. You came with spears after all. I hoped. I am old enough to know better than hope.
lines.direction: calling across the bridge, every word deliberate

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Come, then. Every one of us you kill is one less mouth this winter. Your mayor will be so pleased.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Now. Before she says anything else.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fighting is over. On the old stones of the bridge, Mother Skarrow lies where she fell.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Hm. Well fought. My grandson always said the valley would never share. I should have listened to him.
lines.direction: barely a whisper, a dry laugh in it

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: There was a song I meant to teach somebody. Too late now. It goes into the river with me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last of the clan fall back into the hills, carrying their small ones. None of them look back.

options.label: Tell me the song.
Captain. There's something you should know about that first morning.
It's over.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Seven went up where the wall meets the sky. No. Not for you. Not for the ones with spears.
lines.direction: a breath of melody, then nothing

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She does not speak again.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Children. Our lads shot at children.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: And we've just finished what they started. Gods help me.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: The road's open. That's what we came for.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Funny. I thought this would feel like something.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The clan is leaving the bridge, carrying their tents down to the bank. Not all of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A knot of young goblins holds the middle span, faces painted red, spears levelled. Their war cry is a name. Vorga.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: My grandson's friends. They would rather die on the stones than eat valley bread. Foolish children.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Do what you must. But I have buried enough of them this year. Leave me some to scold.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Truce or no truce, they're on my bridge. Ready when you are.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last of the hotheads flee east along the road, toward the far hills, and Vorga, wherever he is.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: They will go to him. He will tell them they were brave. They were. Brave is cheap this winter.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Bridge is clear. Carts can cross by noon.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: I wanted her dead, you know. For Coll and Annet. I still might, some days.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: But I've never seen goblins carry their own children off a bridge before. I'll think on it.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Your captain thinks. Good. Tell her to think about the grain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Downstream of the bridge, the bank is grey and bare for a mile. Nothing has grown here in a hundred years but one crooked hut.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is hung with charms of bone and river glass that click in the steam. Someone inside is laughing at you.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Took you long enough. A hundred years I've sat here, and finally somebody comes knocking with a sensible face.
lines.direction: papery, unhurried; a cackle that turns into a cough

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Go on, then. Ask me. Everybody asks the wrong thing, so I'll forgive you the first one.

options.label: You were here when the ember fell?
Maud. It's me, from up the bank.
Corvin Ashby told me to find you.
We made peace with Mother Skarrow.
Mother Skarrow is dead.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Ah, there's my quiet neighbour. Never warmed your hands at the wrong fire, did you? That's why you can still think.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: I told you a name once. You wrote it down, I watched you. Kept it safe, have you?

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Corvin! Still counting his missing years, is he? Good boy. Reads by the wrong lamp, but a good boy.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Did you now. She and I are the last two in this valley who remember what we were told. Mind you keep her breathing.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Oh, dearie. She was the other one. The other one who still remembered. Now there's only me, and I'm tired.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Seven years old, I was, and up past my bedtime. The sky went red over the Keep, and the stars came down.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: It didn't fall, dearie. It was thrown.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Falling things tumble. This came down straight, like a stone from a hand. Hissed in the river all night long.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: And I'll tell you something else, since you've a sensible face. I saw who was standing on the hill when it came down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her finger, crooked as a root, points past you across the steaming water. Someone in a deep hood stands on the far bank.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: That one. Same hood. Same face under it. A hundred years, and not one day older. I was seven, dearie, not blind.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: You remember well, Maud. Better than anyone. That was always going to be a problem for somebody.
lines.direction: carrying across the water; faintly amused, faintly sad

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Steam rolls up off the river. When it clears, the far bank is empty.

options.label: Who are they?
Where did they go?

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: If I knew that, dearie, I'd not have spent a century watching the water. Ask them. They'll answer you sideways.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You catch a grey shape on the bridge road, walking toward the docks, unhurried. It leaves no footprints in the ash.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There is nothing. No footprints in the ash, no sound but the river and Maud's charms clicking in the wind.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: I never once warmed my hands at that fire in the river. Think on why I'm the one who remembers.

lines.speaker: old_maud
lines.text: Go on. Come back when you've better questions. I'll still be here. It's the one thing I'm good at.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The town council meets in the back room of the Last Coal. It is warmer in here than the council deserves.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Friends, the road is open and the carts are crossing. Let's thank our heroes, and then let's talk about anything else.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: The goblins, Halden. They want feeding. We gave our word.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: Our word? I don't recall giving mine. And they are, if we're being precise, my granaries.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: Of course the clan can have grain. Everything has a price. The question is who pays it, and the town is already so deep in my ledgers.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: The chapel can spare its tithe barley. It isn't much. But no one sent to my door has ever been turned away.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: It isn't enough, Mother. If we feed the hills, we're short by spring. I've done the sums.

options.label: You've done these sums before, haven't you?
Lady Marrowby. Your family would want this handled quietly.
Mother Aubrine, if the chapel gives first, the rest will be shamed into it.
Then the town eats a little less. That was the deal.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: Clever. You have been listening to me. Yes, a quiet arrangement. Lent at interest, of course, and the mayor signs.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: People ask me what I remember of the night the Keep fell. I was there, I'm told. It's all smoke to me.
lines.direction: light, as if it were a joke

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: You always did find the sharp end of a sermon. Very well. The chapel opens its stores first, and in public.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: Then we shall see who in this room is willing to be seen giving less than the church.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Halden's hand lies flat on a ledger he has not opened. He knows the numbers without looking. He has known them a long time.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: A mayor does a great many sums, friend. Most of them come out badly. That's the job.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Halden. You locked those gates in the spring, before the clan ever came down. I want to know why.
lines.direction: her patience goes all at once

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Because the ground is cooling. The ember under the ford is going out. I've known for six years.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: Every winter the warm fields give a little less. I measured it. I told no one, because if I had, half the town would have left.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: So I locked the grain, let the hills go hungry, and called it prudence. I'm sorry it took goblins to get it out of me.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Six years. I've sat at your table for six years.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: We were all warming our hands at a fire you knew was dying. Gods forgive you, Halden. I'm not sure I can, yet.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: Well. That does change the interest, doesn't it.

options.label: Open the granaries. All of them.
Lady Marrowby, lend it without interest.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: Without interest. How very novel. Very well, for this winter. You'll owe me a favour instead, and I never forget a favour.

lines.speaker: celandine_marrowby
lines.text: No, I don't think so. But I'll lend it gladly. The mayor can sign, now we all know what his signature is worth.

lines.speaker: halden_varrow
lines.text: The granaries open tomorrow. One sack in four goes up the hill, every week. Dagna, will you see it carried?

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Aye. Somebody has to count the sacks honestly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Night in the hills. The first sacks of valley grain came up today, and for once there is a pot over the clan's fire.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Children who were silent a week ago chase each other round the tents, shrieking. Mother Skarrow pretends not to notice.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Sit. You are guests now, which is worse than enemies. Guests we have to feed.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: When the bellies are full, the clan sings. Tonight I sing the old one, because my bones say I should.

options.label: We'd be honoured.
I know a Warden song about seven who crossed the Greywall.
I came over the Greywall too, as a child.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: The valley song. Seven went over, seven came home, they brought something heavy. Yes. Pretty.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Your song was made by the ones who came home. Ours was made by the ones who watched them come.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Hm. I thought you smelled wrong. Not bad. Only far. Like snow from the other side.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Then listen close. This song is about your side of the mountain, a little. Perhaps it is about you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She closes her eyes. Around the fire the clan goes still, and then, low, begins to hum.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Seven went up where the wall meets the sky, seven with nothing, and hungry, and cold.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Seven came down when the snow was still falling, seven came down with their hands full of gold.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: But nobody runs when they carry a fortune. Seven came down, and the seven came running.
lines.direction: sung, faster, the humming rising under it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She stops. The humming stops with her. The fire pops, very loud.

options.label: What were they running from?
Please. Sing us the rest.
I'll ask her in the hill tongue, as family would.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: That is the next verse. And the next verse is not for strangers.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: You fed my children. That makes you something. Not family. Not yet. Come back when you are.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: You ask well. So, a crumb. In the old song the gold is not gold. We sing gold because it rhymes, and the true word is sad.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: The rest when you are family. Not before. Now eat. You are too thin for valley people.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By night the river docks belong to the Ash Market. Lanterns float on the water, and nobody uses their real name.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Down here. Under the third pier, past the eel traps. I don't know how I know that. I've never been under here.
lines.direction: slow and old, then bright and frightened

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Beneath the pier the river runs shallow over black stone. Something glows in the riverbed, dull red, like a coal at the bottom of a grate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ford's ember. It is the size of a cart wheel, and it is cracked and chipped all over, as if something has been gnawing it.

options.label: Those are chisel marks. Someone works this from a boat.
That's the same fire as Tobin's forge.
Someone's been cutting pieces off it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You know these moorings. Ropes worn smooth, and a flat skiff tied where no fisherman would tie it. Somebody comes here often.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You know this heat. It is Tobin's forge-fire, the same colour, the same smell, only vast, and failing.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Careful. You're standing on my livelihood.
lines.direction: dry, unhurried, out of the dark

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A lean figure steps off a skiff onto the black stone, lantern in hand. A river coat, and an easy smile that costs extra.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Rook. I run the Ash Market. You've bought from me, or your grandmother did. Everyone has.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Yes, we chip her. A shard here, a shard there, and somebody's hearth stays warm. Shame to let it go to waste in the mud.

options.label: You're killing it.
Rook. About that job that went wrong.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: She was dying long before I came. I sell the pieces before they're worth nothing. That's not murder. That's timing.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Here's something for free, since I'm feeling generous. I sell more shards than this ember has to give.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Somebody else supplies the difference. I don't know who. I'd like to, before they decide they don't need me.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: There you are. Wondered when the river would bring you back. You still owe me, you know.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Here's how you pay. I'm selling the Kindled more shards than exist in the Vale. Find who's supplying the rest, and we're square.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: It's so cold now. It was warm here, once. I remember it being warm.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: No. I don't. Somebody does.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next morning a crowd gathers by the chapel steps. A woman in a plain grey coat is speaking, and nobody is leaving.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: You've felt how cold it's getting. The fields. The forges. Your own hearths, a little lower every year.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: It doesn't have to be this way. The Hearthflame can burn again. It wants to. It only needs us to be brave enough to feed it.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: Maren Sorrel. I put you out of my chapel once. Don't make me do it to the whole square.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Mother Aubrine. You fed half this town last winter, and you'll bury the other half this one. I'm offering more than prayers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Maren's eyes find you in the crowd. She smiles as if you are old friends.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: You found it, didn't you? Under the docks. I can see it on you. Tell me, what did the ford cost you?

options.label: An old goblin's life.
A share of the town's grain.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Then you understand already. Sometimes one life buys a winter for a thousand. That isn't cruelty. It's arithmetic.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Grain for peace. That's beautiful, truly. And when the grain runs out, and the ground goes cold? Kindness won't warm it.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Come and find me when you're ready to save the Vale, and not only this town. I'll be wherever the embers are.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: Be careful of her. The worst of it is that she believes every word.

options.label: Mother, I need to read the church's oldest scriptures.
We'll be careful.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: The cellar texts? No one has read those in my lifetime. They're very old, and very dull, I'm told.

lines.speaker: mother_aubrine
lines.text: But you came home when I wrote to you. Here. The archive key. Bring it back, and bring me what you find.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crowd breaks up slowly. More than a few of them keep looking back the way Maren went.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night the docks are quiet. The hooded figure waits at the end of the third pier, as if you had arranged to meet.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: You found her. Good. She hasn't long, you know. Cracked and chipped, and cold at the heart. Like most things in this valley.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: She isn't the only one. There are four more. You'll want to reach them before the woman in grey does.

options.label: Who are you?
Why tell us?
You know where I come from, don't you?

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Someone who has watched a great many rivers. You're asking the right questions. You're just asking the wrong people.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Because you came to a bridge and chose. Most people let the choosing happen to them. It matters more than you'd think.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: I know the road you came by. It's longer than you remember. Don't ask me to walk it with you. Not yet.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: The nearest lies in Mirewood, where the marsh began to dream. The Court there will want something for it.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Whatever they ask for, think before you say yes. Things given in Mirewood stay given.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lantern on the pier gutters. When it steadies, you are alone with the sound of the river.
